lawyer:
Mr. Enamul Haque, Advocated ------ For the condemned-prisoner 
Mr. S.B. Barua Advocated ------ For the State
full_judgment: 11. Mr. Enamul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused, submits that there is admittedly no eye-witness and circumstantial evidence are not at all conclusive so as to bring home the charge of murder against the accused Badaruddin. The learned Advocate submits that besides the fact that deceased Monowara Khatoon died in the house of her husband, there is absolutely no evidence so as to connect the convict with the commission of murder. The death of Monowara Khatoon in the house of her husband may give rise to presumption of the guilt of Monowara, but presumption, however strong, cannot take the place of proof. P.W.4 of course, saw Badaruddin beating his wife in the evening and what type of beating it was and what is the motive behind it could not be ascertained from the evidence. The witnesses did not speak of any injuries. The Doctor also did not find any injury on the body of Monowara Khatoon which can be said to have been caused by lathi. The witness said that Wahab went to the house of Badaruddin but did not speak about the presence of witness No. 4 Kashem. P.W.5 stated that the accused did not say anything on being asked. The evidence of P.W.s. 4, 5 and 6 stating that they went to the place of occurrence are contradictory, but they also do not inspire any confidence so as to hold the accused guilty. The A learned trial court found from the conduct of the accused that the accused and he alone was responsible for the murder. This finding of the learned trial court is not based on evidence but on conjecture only. The conduct of the accused cannot be accepted as the basis of conviction, but it could only lend support of art net evidence if there be strong evidence, oral or circumstantial, besides the conduct. The learned trial court also in absence of evidence, has relied on the fact that the accused remained absconding. Remaining absconding after the murder and hided for long time, though relevant, but it is nor conclusive for the guilt of murder. In an unreported judgment in Criminal Appeal No.22 of 1985 which finds mention in the ease reported in 11 BLD (AD) 317 wherein the wife was in the house of her husband and the defence could not give any explanation as to how the deceased died, the husband was acquitted as the witnesses did not say anything.
